messages:
alex: Quick check — planning to convert the redis Deployment -> StatefulSet so each replica gets its own PVC. Target: replicas=2, do a canary using partitioning. Thinking to keep HPA off for this service (redis warm-up is expensive). Will open TF + k8s PRs shortly. Any obvious blockers?

maya: Why remove HPA? Are we confident traffic is stable enough? HPA prevented capacity issues before.

alex: @maya traffic is pretty steady; the problem we saw was scale-down then scale-up causing cache cold starts and OOMs. For Redis it's safer to keep fixed replicas and handle bursts via a dedicated burst pool.

sam: Quick question on canary: StatefulSet partition semantics are weird — which ordinal stays old? we should confirm before rolling.

li: Agree we shouldn't guess. Also check storageclass IO profile and reclaimPolicy.

alex: I tested locally: ordinals start at 0. If replicas=3 and partition=2, only pod-2 will be updated (so highest ordinal acts as canary). For replicas=2 we should use partition=1 to keep pod-0 old and update pod-1 as canary. I'll include that in the manifest.

maya: Add a preStop sleep (15s) to allow conn drain, readiness probe change to tcp-socket on 6379, and terminationGracePeriodSeconds=60. Also set resources: requests cpu 500m / memory 2Gi.

alex: Manifest snippet I'll apply in k8s PR:

```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: StatefulSet
metadata:
  name: redis-cache
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: redis-cache
  serviceName: redis-cache-svc
  updateStrategy:
    type: RollingUpdate
    rollingUpdate:
      partition: 1   # canary: only pod-1 updates
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: redis-cache
    spec:
      terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 60
      containers:
      - name: redis
        image: redis:7.2-alpine
        ports:
        - containerPort: 6379
        readinessProbe:
          tcpSocket:
            port: 6379
          initialDelaySeconds: 5
          periodSeconds: 5
        lifecycle:
          preStop:
            exec:
              command: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "sleep 15"]
        resources:
          requests:
            cpu: "500m"
            memory: "2Gi"
        volumeMounts:
        - name: data
          mountPath: /data
  volumeClaimTemplates:
  - metadata:
      name: data
    spec:
      storageClassName: rredis-fast-io
      accessModes: ["ReadWriteOnce"]
      resources:
        requests:
          storage: 50Gi
```

alex: I'll also update Terraform which currently renders the k8s_manifest for this service. PRs: k8s#4321 (manifest) and tf#789 (k8s_manifest + storageclass). infra-bot should link the PRs.

infra-bot: PR created: https://git.internal.redwood/k8s/pull/4321 and https://git.internal.redwood/infra/pull/789 :github: 

sam: LGTM from infra side. Ping @infra-oncall for drain window and let ops know about PVCs. Also remember to update the docs/rollback steps.

maya: Reviewing now, small nit: bump requests to 700m cpu if we see contention. Otherwise :+1:.

li: Approve after we add a snapshot schedule for the PVCs and note the rollback steps in the TF PR.

alex: Thanks all — will merge canary today, monitor metrics (latency, errors, pod restart count) for 30m, then move partition to 0 to finish rollout if green. Will post updates in this thread. :thumbsup:
